S2.01.needs: none for the signed-out check; a Free account for the signed-in check
S2.01.note: An earlier run recorded that a signed-in visit to / showed Something Went Wrong (E085); the signed-out homepage was not tested earlier.

Look at the first screen for the 'Try chat' button and the Desktop call to action beside it.
Compare with Expected: sign-in, try and download calls to action are visible on the homepage.
Click the Products menu in the header.
Click Chat.
Read the page headline and the paragraph about chatting with eligible models.
Compare with Expected: the page explains the chat assistant and has a 'Try chat' button to start.

Click Deep research.
Look for the section 'Review and edit before you start' and the cited-report explanation.
Compare with Expected: the page explains deep research with cited reports and how to use it.
Click the Products menu in the header.
Click Work.
Read the menu description 'A goal in, a plan first, approvals on sensitive steps' and the page that opens.
Compare with Expected: the page presents agentic work and has a way to start.
Click the Products menu in the header.
Click Code.
Read the menu description 'One coding agent across the CLI and VS Code' and the page that opens.
Compare with Expected: the page presents the coding agent and how to get it.

Click Desktop.
Read the page on what the desktop app does and which platforms it covers.
Compare with Expected: the page describes the desktop app truthfully, including availability and download.
Click the Products menu in the header.
Click Mobile.
Read the page on the mobile app and its availability.
Compare with Expected: the page describes the mobile app and its availability.

Click CLI.
Find the install section and the install command, if the page shows one.
Compare with Expected: the page tells a visitor how to install the CLI and offers a working install.

Click Code for VS Code.
Read the page describing the extension and its availability.
Compare with Expected: the page describes the IDE extension and where it is available.

Click Extension.

Click MCP directory.
Type a server name in the search box and read the results.
Open one listing and read its publisher and listed tools.

Under Product, click Plugins.
Browse the plugin catalogue and click one plugin name.
Compare with Expected: a logged-out visitor can browse the catalogue with a path to install.

S2.16.note: An earlier run recorded that /skills opened Settings > Skills for a signed-in user; the signed-out directory in apps/web/app/skills/SignedOutSkills.tsx was not tested earlier.
steps: Click the Resources menu in the header or scroll to the footer Resources column.
Click Skills.
Look for the heading 'Skills live in your workspace' and the skill list.
Compare with Expected: a logged-out visitor sees a public skill directory.

Under Product, click Gallery.
Look at the template cards and the 'Start from scratch' option.
Compare with Expected: the gallery offers curated templates that can be previewed and launched into chat.

Under Product, click Plugins, then click any plugin name.

Under Product, click Gallery, then click any template card.
Check that the page address shows /gallery/ followed by the template name.

S2.22.needs: none to view; a Free account to reach the checkout step
S2.22.note: Paid plan buttons open checkout; the tester must stop before payment.
steps: Scroll to the footer and find the Product column.
Click Pricing.
Read the individual plan cards, their prices and the plan names.
Click a paid plan's button and stop at the checkout or sign-in step. Do not complete a purchase.
Compare with Expected: individual plans and prices are listed, and a plan can be chosen.

S2.23.needs: none to view; a Free account to reach the checkout step
S2.23.note: The Teams page button text is built from a seat constant, so its exact words are composed; 'Get Team' is the pricing page's button key.
steps: Click the Solutions menu in the header.
Click Teams.
Click the button that starts at the minimum seat count, which opens the Team pricing section.
Choose a seat count and read the per-seat price.
Compare with Expected: per-seat pricing is shown, and the buyer can choose seats. Stop before paying.
Click the Solutions menu in the header.
Click Enterprise.
Look for the 'Start the evaluation' section and its contact or sales button.
Compare with Expected: the Enterprise offering is presented with a sales path. Do not submit the form.

Scroll to the 'Compare plans' section.
Read the rows and the plan columns.
Compare each cell with Expected: the cell should match what the plan allows.

Open the article 'Usage limits, credits and top-ups'.
Read how usage is measured and what happens when an allowance runs out.
Also open Pricing and read the sentence 'Weekly and monthly usage allowances apply.'
Compare with Expected: public pages explain managed usage, allowances and credits.

Click Downloads.

Compare with Expected: installers are offered per platform and architecture, and only what is published is shown.

steps: Click the Resources menu in the header.
Click Documentation.

Click "Share…", then choose a public link and create it (the dialog title reads "Share conversation" until a link exists).

Check that the shared conversation appears read-only with its messages, compared with Expected (a logged-out visitor sees shared content).
